Subject: Production: sudden latency + hallucination spike after qprofile upgrade

Naomi,

We just observed a sharp regression in production after the quantization profile bump last night (you mentioned vQ-2.1). Key symptoms: p95 token latency jumped from ~220ms to ~1.5s, end-to-end throughput dropped ~27%, and our automated quality checks show a 3x increase in hallucination flags on the top-1 answers. Error rates (5xx) increased from 0.8% to ~4.6% in the last hour.

Our SRE team attached a short log excerpt and metric snapshot (see attachment: request_log_excerpt.json). This is impacting our critical billing flows — we have customers timing out. Please escalate and advise next steps; immediate rollback would be ideal if that’s the safest path.

Time is sensitive; we’re ready to hop on a call.

Thanks,
Alicia Ramos
Director of Product
Summit Insight

Naomi / team — investigating now. Notes from early triage:
- vQ-2.1 rolled 2026-09-29T23:40:12Z to Summit’s production pool. The change set included a new reduced-precision kernel path for MatMul that falls back to an alternate kernel when sequence length > 256.
- Our perf sims during onboarding did not hit the same sequence-length distribution Summit sees; initial theory: the fallback path is hitting more frequently and is not yet optimized, causing the per-token time increase. That explains latency and throughput drop.
- The hallucination bump is concerning — may be correlated if KV-cache alignment or rounding introduced occasional decoding perturbations. We’re running unit regressions.

Immediate plan (approved if no objections):
1) Execute an emergency rollback of Summit’s serving pool to vQ-2.0 (fully revert) — estimated 30 min to cutover and validate.
2) While rollback proceeds, collect perf diffs (will attach) and run targeted unit tests against Summit message traces to reproduce hallucination cases.
3) If rollback is not acceptable, we can do a 10% canary rollback within 10 minutes to validate impact before full roll.

I’m pushing a hotfix branch to disable the new kernel fallback and will post perf-diff.txt in ~20 minutes.

—Rishi
Sr. Eng Manager, Inference Runtime
Redwood Inference

Alicia — final update. We executed a full rollback to vQ-2.0 against Summit’s production pool at 2026-10-01T16:20:00Z. Validation and steady-state checks completed at 2026-10-01T17:10:00Z.

Post-rollback metrics (summaries attached to this thread):
- p95 token latency: restored to 240ms (pre-regression ~220ms)
- Throughput: recovered to +25% vs worst of spike (within expected variance of baseline)
- 5xx errors: dropped back to 0.9%
- Automated hallucination flags: back to baseline levels

Rishi’s team will continue a focused root-cause investigation on the kernel fallback. We will provide a post-mortem and a plan for a corrected vQ-2.1 candidate with additional sequence-length safety checks and deterministic unit tests prior to any future rollout to Summit.

Thank you for your patience — I’ll schedule a follow-up call tomorrow to walk through the timeline and next steps; Marissa will reach out with a meeting invite and credit documentation.
